articles.title: Ketamine, an interoceptive associative agent? Evidence from ketamine-assisted Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement for opioid use disorder.
articles.abstract: Relapse in opioid use disorder (OUD) remains common despite pharmacotherapy. Altered interoceptive processing may contribute to addiction, and ketamine-induced changes in salience and insula-related networks may facilitate mindfulness-based interoceptive learning. This secondary analysis examined whether ketamine-assisted psychotherapy (KAP) added to Mindfulness-Oriented Recovery Enhancement (MORE) improved interoceptive awareness and whether these changes mediated reductions in opioid craving. Sixty-eight adults with OUD receiving buprenorphine were randomized to 8 weeks of MORE with or without KAP. Assignment was unblinded, and outcomes were self-reported. Interoception was assessed using ecological momentary assessment (EMA) of body awareness and Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA) subscales. Posttreatment EMA data were available for 18 MORE + KAP and 15 MORE participants. Mixed-effects models and path analysis were conducted. Piecewise modeling showed a greater increase in EMA-assessed body awareness salience in MORE + KAP during days 1-35, spanning the pre-dosing and first-ketamine-dose period ( Adjunctive ketamine was associated with rapid, sustained increases in body awareness salience. Improvements in interoceptive regulatory capacity mediated reduced opioid craving, supporting interoception as a potential mechanism and treatment target in ketamine-augmented mindfulness interventions for OUD. gov:NCT04892251.

articles.title: Intravenous Ketamine or Esketamine in Adolescents With Major Depressive Disorder: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy and safety of intravenous ketamine or esketamine in adolescents with major depressive disorder (MDD) remain insufficiently defined. This systematic review of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) aimed to evaluate the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of intravenous ketamine or esketamine in this population. A comprehensive search of four international databases (PubMed, EMBASE, PsycINFO, and the Cochrane Library) was conducted to identify RCTs comparing intravenous ketamine or esketamine with intravenous midazolam in adolescents with MDD. Three RCTs involving a total of 134 adolescents with MDD were included. Two trials assessed the antidepressant effects of intravenous ketamine compared with intravenous midazolam, with inconsistent findings. No significant advantage of intravenous ketamine over intravenous midazolam was observed in reducing anxiety symptoms (1 RCT). One trial compared intravenous esketamine with intravenous midazolam and evaluated antidepressant, anti-suicidal, and neurocognitive outcomes, demonstrating the superiority of intravenous esketamine. Both intravenous ketamine and intravenous esketamine were associated with significantly higher rates of dissociative symptoms (1 RCT each), and intravenous esketamine was also linked to a higher incidence of psychopathological symptoms (1 RCT). Systematic reporting of adverse events was provided in only one of the three included RCTs. Given the limited number of studies, small sample sizes, and methodological heterogeneity of the available RCTs, the current evidence base remains preliminary and insufficient to support definitive conclusions regarding the efficacy and safety of intravenous ketamine/esketamine in adolescents with MDD. These findings highlight the need for further adequately powered RCTs to establish robust and clinically meaningful evidence.

articles.title: Integrating multi-receptor and neuron-glia mechanisms of ketamine's antidepressant action: a convergence framework for understanding efficacy.
articles.abstract: Ketamine has revolutionized psych iatric treatment, challenging monoamine-based paradigms through its capacity for rapid antidepressant action. While N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR) antagonism remains the canonical mechanism, this integrative review proposes a multi-receptor, neuron-glia convergence model to help account for ketamine's therapeutic efficacy. We outline the well-established disinhibition cascade, whereby preferential NMDAR blockade on GABAergic interneurons induces cortical disinhibition, triggering a transient glutamate surge and subsequent α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptor activation. Furthermore, we discuss emerging, albeit indirect reports suggesting that ketamine and its metabolites may interact with the tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) transmembrane domain and modulate TrkB-related signaling. Beyond neurons, we consider the contributions of glial cells, particularly astrocytes, microglia, and oligodendrocyte lineage cells, as players in ketamine response in antidepressant effects. We further discuss evidence for opioid context-dependent effects that, at present, are insufficient to account for ketamine's broader antidepressant effects. Finally, we highlighted the sigma-1 receptor (S1R) as a chaperone modulator of ketamine-induced sustained neuroplasticity and intercellular neuron-glia communication. Collectively, the available data suggest that ketamine's efficacy likely arises from convergent actions across multiple molecular targets and both neuronal and glial cell types. Importantly, many components of this model remain hypothetical and require rigorous

articles.title: Intermittent theta burst stimulation to extend early ketamine response in treatment-resistant depression: A preliminary enriched randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
articles.abstract: Ketamine produces rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant depression (TRD), but these benefits diminish within days. Whether intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS) can sustain ketamine response and whether such effects are associated with changes in large-scale brain networks are unclear. Adults with TRD who exhibited an antidepressant response to two low-dose ketamine infusions (0.5 mg/kg) were randomized to 5 days of accelerated iTBS or sham stimulation. The primary outcome was the change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) scores across the Phase 2 period through Day 49. Resting-state functional MRI was obtained at baseline and after the stimulation course to examine thalamocortical and corticostriatal connectivity. Among 45 enrolled participants, 5 did not complete ketamine induction and 2 withdrew before randomization. Thirty-eight were randomized to active iTBS (n = 19) or sham iTBS (n = 19), and 37 completed follow-up through Day 49 (non-completion rate, 17.8%). In the intention-to-treat analysis, the Phase 2 mixed-effects model showed a significant overall group effect favoring active iTBS (P = 0.020), without a significant group × time interaction. Exploratory remission rates were higher with active iTBS at Days 15 and 29. Response maintenance favored active iTBS but did not reach statistical significance (log-rank P = 0.063). Exploratory fMRI analyses in 15 participants suggested differential group-by-time changes in thalamocortical and corticostriatal connectivity. In this enriched trial, ketamine infusion followed by iTBS was associated with lower overall depressive symptom severity during the randomized follow-up period through Day 49 among early ketamine responders. Exploratory fMRI analyses suggested treatment-related network changes.

articles.title: From Toad Venom to Drug Development: The Clinical Pharmacology of Mebufotenin (5-MeO-DMT) in Treatment-Resistant Depression.
articles.abstract: Treatment-resistant depression affects about one-third of patients with major depressive disorder and remains a major unmet need. This narrative review analyses its clinical pharmacology, drawing on a structured search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, Scopus, ClinicalTrials.gov and grey literature through 15 August 2026, supplemented by regulatory and sponsor disclosures. articles.title: Exploring the durability of esketamine and ketamine's antidepressant effects in the maintenance phase of treatment: A systematic review.
articles.abstract: Ketamine has shown rapid antidepressant effects in treatment-resistant mood disorders; however, the durability of these benefits during maintenance treatment remains unclear. This systematic review evaluated outcomes associated with repeated ketamine and esketamine administration during the maintenance phase of treatment. A systematic search of PubMed, Ovid, and Scopus was conducted from database inception through March 2026. Studies involving more than 8 treatments or more than 1 month of treatment in individuals with mood disorders were included. Eligible designs consisted of randomized controlled trials, open-label studies, observational cohorts, and case series. A total of 43 studies met inclusion criteria, including randomized controlled trials and extension studies (n = 8), open-label studies (n = 4), observational studies (n = 24), and case series (n = 7). Overall, ketamine and esketamine were associated with sustained clinical improvement during ongoing treatment, although outcomes varied across study designs. Randomized trials demonstrated reduced relapse rates with continued treatment, while relapse was common following discontinuation of treatment. Observational studies showed heterogeneous outcomes, with evidence of both sustained improvement and attenuation of benefit over time. Case series reported mixed durability. These findings suggest that continued treatment may be important for preserving therapeutic benefit, although long-term outcomes are not uniform across individuals. Further research is needed to optimize maintenance strategies, identify predictors of sustained response, and clarify the long-term efficacy and safety of ketamine-based therapies for mood disorders.

articles.title: Ketamine/Esketamine in Clinical Practice: Areas of Consensus and Nonconsensus from an American Society of Clinical Psychopharmacology (ASCP) Delphi Panel Task Force.
Next-Generation Psychedelic Drug Development.
articles.abstract: Psychedelic medicine has gained rapid popularity for the treatment of a variety of neuropsychiatric disorders, including depression, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder. As novel psychedelic analogues and treatment regimes emerge, increasing numbers of variables are being tested. Here, we review various approaches and considerations for novel psychedelic therapies, including the strengths and limitations of current assays and models. Finally, we provide guidance and considerations for next-generation psychedelic drug development.

articles.title: Bridging Nonconsecutive Esketamine Weeks with Bupropion and Over-the-Counter Dextromethorphan.
articles.abstract: Frequent clinic visits required for maintenance intranasal (IN) esketamine therapy can limit treatment feasibility. Our case presents a 52-year-old woman with treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and bipolar II disorder (BD-II) who achieved sustained remission with weekly esketamine, but consistently experienced relapse of depressive symptoms when treatment intervals extended beyond 10 days. Her Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) score decreased from 27 at baseline to 4 (±1) during maintenance treatment; however, with even a single delayed session, her PHQ-9 score could increase by as many as 8 points (from 4 to 12). To prevent relapse when she could not receive esketamine weekly, she began taking over-the-counter (OTC) dextromethorphan (DXM) and continued bupropion extended-release (XL), which she started prior to esketamine treatment. With 45 mg twice daily (BID) DXM and 450 mg daily bupropion XL, she was able to tolerate every-other-week administration of esketamine without depressive relapse. DXM and esketamine are both believed to function via antagonism of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. Bupropion is a competitive inhibitor of cytochrome P450 2D6 (CYP2D6), which is involved in the metabolism of DXM and maintenance of serum DXM concentration.

articles.title: Brain network-driven predictive neural markers for suicide risk.
articles.abstract: Suicide is a significant public health challenge, underscoring the need for temporally precise and objective biomarkers to identify acute suicide risk. One potential biomarker is electrophysiological brain connectivity measured by magnetoencephalography (MEG). This study used publicly available atlases to estimate parcel-level within-network connectivity. The multi-omics statistical method was applied to assess whether canonical networks-including the default mode (DMN), executive control (ECN), and salience (SN) networks-could differentiate individuals experiencing a recent suicidal crisis (high risk) from those with a history of suicide attempts but not in the past year (lower risk), clinical controls with depression but no history of suicide risk (clinical controls), and individuals with no personal or family history of either psychiatric disorder or suicidal behavior (minimal risk). The high risk group exhibited significantly weaker functional connectivity within specific regions of these networks ( These findings highlight critical brain regions and network interactions, advancing our understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying suicide risk. Leveraging electrophysiological connectivity and innovative tools may help develop targeted interventions and early identification strategies for those at heightened risk of suicide. www.clinicaltrials.gov, identifier NCT02543983.

articles.title: From Evidence to Practice: A Systematic Review of Implementation of Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy.
articles.abstract: Evidence supporting psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy (PAP) for treating posttraumatic stress disorder, depression, and other historically difficult to treat mental health disorders is growing rapidly. Interest from the public and within the US government to provide access to these treatments has also grown. Considering the gap between discovery of effective treatments and implementing them in clinical settings, it is important to synthesize current knowledge of implementing these complex treatment modalities to aid efforts for systematic implementation going forward. The specific objectives of this systematic review were to: (1) identify extant literature on implementation of PAP, and (2) synthesize and present findings to understand current implementation knowledge and inform future directions. This systematic review followed the procedures outlined in Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020. Six databases were searched using a string developed with the keywords "implementation," "psychedelic (methylenedioxymethamphetamine, psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide, ketamine)," and "psychotherapy" along with Elsevier expansions and synonyms. The study only included peer-reviewed research on PAP, which reported on the implementation of the interventions. The implementation science framework, the Practical, Robust, implementation and Sustainability Model, guided the data extraction and synthesis about implementation-relevant factors. A total of 2,406 articles were identified, and 2,074 of these were screened by title and abstract after the initial elimination of duplicates and sources that were not peer-reviewed research articles (e.g., gray literature). Forty-seven were retrieved for full text review, and 20 studies were included in the review. Most studies (15) were cross-sectional surveys and/or qualitative interviews assessing organizational perspective. The remaining (5) presented included aspects of patient perspective (2), infrastructure (2), and patient characteristics (1). There is a noticeable gap in implementation-focused research on best practices for translating PAP from academic settings into accessible clinical programs. Addressing this gap is essential to support the safe and effective implementation of PAP in real-world settings.

articles.title: Psilocybin-Assisted Therapy for Cancer-Related Psychological and Existential Distress in Adults with Cancer: An Integrative Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: Psilocybin-assisted therapy has reemerged as a promising intervention for distress associated with cancer and life-threatening illness. This integrative systematic review evaluated evidence on the safety, efficacy, and therapeutic impact of psilocybin-assisted therapy in adults with cancer experiencing depression, anxiety and existential distress. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, and CINAHL databases were searched from 10 August 2025 to 31 October 2025. Eleven eligible reports derived from six independent clinical cohorts met inclusion criteria. Psilocybin was generally administered as a single supervised moderate-to-high dose (25-30 mg/70 kg), within structured preparation, dosing, and integration. Across all designs, psilocybin produced rapid and enduring reductions in depression, anxiety, existential distress, and fear of death, with benefits lasting 2-6 months and, in some cases, up to 4.5 years. Qualitative findings highlighted enhanced emotional clarity, acceptance, spiritual well-being, and reconnection with meaning. Five of the 11 reports met Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT) criteria; concerns in others involved assessor blinding, representativeness, confounding control, or mixed-methods integration. No psilocybin-related serious adverse events were reported; transient cardiovascular changes, headache, nausea, anxiety or emotional distress, and occasional brief psychotic-like symptoms occurred. Psilocybin-assisted therapy may be promising but still investigational palliative pharmacotherapy-related intervention for cancer-related psychological and existential distress.

articles.title: The molecular and neurochemical basis of altered intrinsic neural timescales in major depressive disorder: a multimodal imaging-transcriptomic investigation of esketamine and sertraline treatment.
articles.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is characterized by dysfunction in higher-order cortical regions involved in emotional and cognitive processes; however, its neurobiological basis remains unclear. Pharmacological treatments, including esketamine and sertraline, produce rapid antidepressant effects. We investigated the local intrinsic neural dynamics underlying these antidepressant effects using intrinsic neural timescales (INT), which measure the duration and capacity of information integration in localized brain regions. A total of 57 healthy controls and 41 patients with MDD were included. All patients with MDD received six intravenous infusions of esketamine (0.25 mg/kg) and two weeks of sertraline treatment. All participants underwent resting-state fMRI to quantify INT alterations at the voxel and brain network levels, followed by spatial correlation analyses linking autocorrelation metrics of INT signals to transcriptomic data from the Allen Human Brain Atlas and PET-derived neurotransmitter receptor maps. The spatial correlation between PLS2 scores and case-control t-statistic maps did not pass rigorous spin permutation testing (r = 0.484, p = 0.068) and did not meet the conventional significance threshold of 0.05. Accordingly, all subsequent enrichment analyses based on PLS2 results are presented as exploratory preliminary observations for hypothesis generation. Compared with healthy controls, patients with MDD exhibited significantly elevated INT levels in the left and right precuneus. Following treatment, patients with MDD showed significantly increased INT in the left occipital midline region and left calcarine cortex. At the brain network level, INT levels were significantly reduced in the default mode network (DMN) in patients with MDD compared with healthy controls. Compared with the pre-treatment state, the cerebellar network (CN) showed significantly elevated INT levels after treatment. Partial least squares regression analysis suggested potential associations between INT alterations and spatial gene expression gradients particularly those associated with immune responses, hormonal regulation, neutrophils, regulatory T cells, and glutamatergic synapses. Cell-type enrichment analysis identified excitatory and inhibitory neurons as key cellular contributors. Alterations in INT also correlated with cortical 5-HT1b and NAT receptor density, suggesting a role for inhibitory neurotransmission in temporal integration deficits. This study advances understanding of treatment-related brain abnormalities in patients with MDD from the perspective of local neural dynamics. These findings support a multiscale pathophysiological framework involving brain connectivity dynamics, molecular architecture, and neurochemical regulation in MDD.

articles.title: Persisting psychological complications following the use of classic psychedelics: A qualitative study of help-seeking experiences.
articles.abstract: While growing enthusiasm for the therapeutic potential of classic psychedelics has led to a rise in non-clinical use, attention to persisting adverse effects has emerged with delay. A subset of individuals report persisting complications such as hallucinogen persisting perception disorder (HPPD), depersonalization/derealization disorder (DDD), anxiety and depression. Yet few medical services are equipped to address these complications. This qualitative study examines how societal, medical, and media discourses shape the experiences of individuals with persisting psychedelic-related complications, focusing on help-seeking trajectories. Thirteen semi-structured interviews with adults experiencing persisting psychedelic-related psychological symptoms (four women, nine men, age 19-49 years; HPPD ( Three interrelated themes emerged: (1) The dissonance between expectation and harm-idealized media and scientific portrayals of psychedelics shaped initial use and complicated recognition of adverse outcomes; (2) stigma, silence, and self-blame-prohibitionist discourse and internalized shame significantly inhibited help-seeking; and (3) between systemic absence and self-organized support-participants encountered clinical unpreparedness and epistemic dismissal, which often led them to rely on online peer communities and self-management strategies. Positive clinical encounters, characterized by professional expertise and non-judgemental engagement, were experienced as helpful. Adequate clinical and conceptual frameworks for persisting psychedelic-related complications are lacking. An interdisciplinary, experience-informed approach integrating realistic risk communication, clinician training, and destigmatization is required to support affected individuals.

articles.title: Transcriptional profiling of antidepressant ketamine and electroconvulsive therapy treatment.
articles.abstract: Treatment-resistant depression (TRD) affects 30-50% of patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) and sub-anesthetic ketamine treatment can relieve TRD, yet their antidepressant mechanisms remain unclear. We hypothesized that peripheral blood gene expression might offer a non-invasive proxy of potential treatment-response biomarkers. We conducted a transcriptome analysis on peripheral blood samples from individuals with TRD undergoing ECT (N = 37) or serial ketamine infusions (N = 60), and non-depressed controls (N = 35). Samples were collected at baseline and at multiple follow-up time points. Differential gene expression (DGE) at the single gene and network level identified transcriptional changes and co-regulated gene modules associated with diagnosis, treatment, and response/remission status using Weighted Gene Co-Expression Network Analysis (WGCNA), correcting for multiple comparisons. Longitudinal transcriptional changes were not detected for either treatment for individual genes or networks (FDR corrected or |logFC| >0.05). When comparing remitters and non-remitters at baseline in the ketamine group, we observed evidence of enrichment for immune-related functions overall with one gene significantly differentially expressed (i.e., IGKV1-9) (p = 2.5E-05, logFC = -0.51). In the ECT sample, when considering gene networks, we observed significant interaction effects between time and diagnosis. At least six co-regulated gene modules yielded significant differences at baseline between ECT patients and controls. Despite the robust clinical improvements associated with ECT and ketamine, peripheral blood RNA-seq revealed only limited longitudinal gene expression changes. However, pre-treatment differences in gene expression profiles suggest some potential predictive value. Larger samples may be warranted to detect possible peripheral molecular signatures of rapid-acting antidepressant response.

articles.title: Att negera verkligheten - En utforskning av ontologisk chock och psykedeliska erfarenheter : En översiktsstudie
articles.abstract: Background: Psychedelics are currently undergoing a renaissance both within and outside healthcare contexts. There is general agreement that these substances have potential in healthcare, but the risks are still not fully understood. The concept of ontological shock is used sparingly and unclearly, especially for therapeutic purposes. Therefore, we believe there is a knowledge gap to illuminate, which this paper aims to do. articles.title: Update on Sedation for Upper Gastrointestinal Endoscopy in Japan: Current Evidence on Remimazolam.
articles.abstract: Sedation is an essential component of upper gastrointestinal endoscopy because it reduces patient discomfort and anxiety while improving patient acceptance and procedural quality. In Japan, benzodiazepines such as midazolam and opioid analgesics have long been widely used in routine clinical practice; however, many of these agents historically lacked formal insurance approval for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy. Propofol is also a useful sedative because of its rapid onset and recovery, but its use in Japan has been limited because of concerns regarding respiratory and cardiovascular depression and the need for management by anesthesia-trained personnel. Against this background, the approval of remimazolam for sedation during gastrointestinal endoscopy in June 2025 represented a major turning point in Japanese endoscopic sedation practice. Remimazolam is an ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine rapidly metabolized by carboxylesterases and reversible with flumazenil. Japanese phase III trials demonstrated high sedation success rates and rapid recovery during upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, including in elderly patients. Compared with midazolam, remimazolam shortened awakening and ambulation times, whereas compared with propofol, it may cause fewer respiratory and cardiovascular adverse events. This review summarizes the current status of upper gastrointestinal endoscopic sedation in Japan, focusing on the clinical evidence and positioning of the newly approved ultra-short-acting benzodiazepine, remimazolam.

articles.title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
articles.abstract:
Purpose

Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair.

Methods

Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA.

Results

We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+).

Conclusions

Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

articles.title: Glis1 regulates metabolic programming by promoting H3K18 lactylation to alleviate neuronal senescence following spinal cord injury.
articles.abstract: Neuronal senescence is a significant factor impeding spinal cord injury (SCI) repair. Research indicates that Glis1, a Kruppel-like zinc finger transcription factor, is pivotal in reprogramming senescent cells and enhancing genomic stability via lactylation. Histone lactylation, an epigenetic modification using lactate as a substrate, becomes prominent post-SCI due to increased neuronal lactate levels. However, the mechanisms linking neuronal senescence and histone lactylation following SCI remain poorly understood. This study elucidates the roles of Glis1, H3K18 lactylation, and neuronal senescence through comprehensive in vivo and in vitro investigations. The findings reveal a post-SCI rise in neuronal lactate levels, accompanied by cellular senescence. Furthermore, upregulation of Glis1 attenuates senescence and promotes histone lactylation. The downstream target secretogranin II (SCG2), identified via ChIP-seq and RNA-seq, was found to exert negative feedback on glycolytic metabolism and lactylation, thereby suppressing neuronal senescence. These results unveil a novel regulatory mechanism of Glis1 in neuronal senescence following SCI through the p300/H3K18la/SCG2 axis, offering a new therapeutic target for spinal cord repair.

articles.title: A bioactivity-enhanced thermosensitive amnion-derived hydrogel with sustained IGF-1 release: A multitargeted and efficient strategy for corneal injury repair.
articles.abstract: Corneal alkali burn (CAB) remains difficult to treat because rapid tear clearance limits topical drug exposure, while the injured cornea develops a complex microenvironment involving inflammation, neovascularization, fibrosis, epithelial barrier loss, and impaired nerve repair. Here, we developed a human amniotic membrane-derived thermosensitive hydrogel (hAMgel) and loaded it with insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) to create a bioactive sustained-release system (IGF1@hAMgel) for CAB repair. The hAMgel transformed from a flowable precursor into a semi-transparent film on the ocular surface within 1-2 min and IGF1@hAMgel released approximately 90% of loaded IGF-1 over 24 h, with corneal IGF-1 concentration peaking at 2 h post-dose (378.5 pg/mg protein) and remaining detectable over 24 h, supporting sustained topical exposure. In a rat CAB model, IGF1@hAMgel accelerated epithelial healing, reducing the fluorescein-stained area from 31.34 ± 2.83% in controls to 16.78 ± 2.87% at day 1. By day 14, IGF1@hAMgel reduced corneal opacity (0.67 ± 0.52 vs. 4.00 ± 0.00), resolved edema with central corneal thickness approaching baseline (187.7 ± 16.31 μm vs. 178.3 ± 5.89 μm), suppressed neovascularization (CD31-positive area 4.46 ± 1.69% vs. 24.33 ± 2.07%), and promoted corneal nerve regeneration. Proteomic analysis showed that hAMgel retained abundant extracellular matrix(ECM) components, including collagens, Lumican, and fibronectin, together with repair-related and immunomodulatory proteins. These findings identify IGF1@hAMgel as a sutureless, eye-drop-like bioactive ECM platform that integrates growth-factor delivery with amnion-derived reparative cues for multitargeted ocular surface repair.

articles.title: A self-crosslinkable, adhesive intestine-derived extracellular matrix hydrogel enhances organoid retention and restores intestinal barrier integrity.
articles.abstract: Disruption of the intestinal barrier impairs essential functions of the gastrointestinal tract and triggers severe inflammation. Accordingly, transplantation of intestinal organoids restores the integrity of the injured intestinal barrier by promoting regeneration. However, the dynamic mucosal microenvironment of the intestine hinders effective retention of transplanted organoids, thereby limiting their therapeutic efficacy. To address this challenge, this study introduces a pyrogallol (PG)-conjugated intestine-derived extracellular matrix (IEM) (IEM-PG) as a scaffold for effective organoid transplantation. The dual crosslinking of IEM-based fibrillogenesis and oxidative PG coupling enabled IEM-PG to form a robust hydrogel scaffold without crosslinking agents under physiological conditions. Moreover, the IEM-PG hydrogel exhibited enhanced mechanical properties, superior bio-adhesion, and greater resistance to enzymatic degradation than the pristine IEM. The IEM-PG hydrogel was also highly biocompatible and did not adversely affect the viability and development of colonic organoids. The solution-type IEM-PG was readily injected into colonic tissue, thus allowing IEM-PG to initially spread along the intestinal lining. Transplantation of colonic organoids using IEM-PG in a mouse colonic ulcer model demonstrated effective cell retention in the intestinal tract, thereby restoring the structural integrity and function of the intestinal barrier. The study further demonstrated that the patch-type IEM-PG hydrogel was effective for the transplantation of colonic assembloids and the treatment of colonic perforation. Overall, this study presents the IEM engineered with an adhesive motif as a self-crosslinking hydrogel platform for organoid/assembloid transplantation and intestinal tissue repair.

articles.title: Barcoded oligonucleotide system (BOLT) for targeted organ delivery.
articles.abstract: The therapeutic potential of oligonucleotides (oligos) is limited by insufficient delivery to extrahepatic tissues. In vitro assays often fail to accurately predict in vivo behavior, while testing each oligo candidate in animals remains inherently low throughput. Here, we conceive a barcoded oligonucleotide system (BOLT), a platform that enables high-throughput in vivo evaluations of small-molecule ligands and identifies tissue-specific oligo delivery. BOLT integrates rational design of oligo barcodes, modular conjugation chemistry, and next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based quantification, allowing simultaneous evaluation of many chemically diverse ligand-oligo conjugates within a single animal. Notably, this platform is applicable in both mice and nonhuman primates (NHPs). Using BOLT, we discovered ligands with tropism for tissues such as the brain, lung, and muscle. Collectively, these results indicate that the BOLT platform can accelerate the discovery of tissue-targeting ligands for broad oligo therapeutics.

articles.title: Ultrasound-activated piezoelectric muscle constructs for tissue-engineered regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces.
articles.abstract: Regenerative peripheral nerve interfaces (RPNIs) are emerging platforms capable to translate neural activity into controllable myoelectric signals. However, current clinical RPNIs rely on muscle autografts, limiting their scalability and extensive adoption. Here, we report a bioactive, ultrasound-responsive piezoelectric muscle biomaterial designed as a fully tissue-engineered alternative to autologous grafts. The construct consists of fibrinogen-based muscle tissues enriched with barium titanate nanoparticles (BTNPs, diameter∼60 nm) and supported by a biodegradable surgical membrane that promotes the formation of aligned, multinucleated myotubes. The incorporation of BTNPs imparts intrinsic piezoelectric activity to the construct, and the nanoparticles are taken up by developing myotubes, enabling remote mechanoelectrical tissue stimulation under low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS). In vivo, piezoelectric constructs implanted around the rat peroneal nerve for two months undergo LIPUS-driven activation of internalized BTNPs, which enhances muscle maturation, and electromechanical responsiveness, yielding myoelectrical signals up to 3.2 mV upon nerve activation. Histological analyses confirm improved structural organization, increased desmin expression, and evidence of neovascularization and axonal regeneration within the engineered interface. These findings suggest that the piezoelectric constructs form stable, functional biointerfaces with peripheral nerves, and that LIPUS-driven activation of embedded BTNPs provides a non-invasive strategy to potentiate muscle development and signal transduction. This study positions LIPUS-responsive, engineered piezoelectric muscle constructs as a donor-free, bioactive platform alternative to traditional autografts for next-generation human-machine interfaces and regenerative bioelectronics.

articles.title: Targeted Screening of Traditional and Novel Stimulants in Dried Blood Spots Using LC-MS/MS.
articles.abstract: Novel psychoactive substances, such as synthetic cathinones, are constantly evolving. Examples of recently reported substances within this class include eutylone, N,N-dimethylpentylone, N-propyl butylone, and pentylone. Given their occurrence in forensic casework, methods for toxicological analysis of these compounds are needed. The application of dried blood spots (DBS) to the analysis of traditional and novel stimulants provides multiple benefits such as low volume needed for sampling and facilitated transportation and storage. This chapter describes a fast and simple procedure for the simultaneous screening of traditional stimulants (amphetamine, methamphetamine, MDMA, MDA and cocaine) and synthetic cathinones (eutylone, N,N-dimethylpentylone, N-propyl butylone and pentylone) in DBS using liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).

articles.title: Determination of Tryptamines in Biological Specimens.
articles.abstract: Tryptamines constitute a class of organic compounds structurally derived from tryptamine, a natural alkaloid found in plants, fungi, and the human body. This group encompasses biologically significant molecules such as serotonin and melatonin, as well as psychoactive compounds like DMT and psilocybin. Tryptamines are typically classified into simple tryptamines and ergolines, with further subclassifications based on structural modifications on the indole ring system. Their primary mechanism of action involves modulation of serotonergic receptors, especially the 5-HT2A, often resulting in psychedelic effects. While some tryptamines are naturally occurring, others are synthetically produced and increasingly encountered as new psychoactive substances. The study presents a rapid and robust LC-MS/MS method for the simultaneous detection and quantification of 37 tryptamines in human urine and plasma. The method employs a ThermoFisher UHPLC-LC-MS/MS system using a Hypersil GOLD C18 column and gradient elution, with MS^n acquisition in positive ESI mode. Analytical validation demonstrated high selectivity, sensitivity, and reproducibility. Sample preparation was performed through a combination of liquid-liquid and protein precipitation extraction procedures. The method successfully identified tryptamines using product ion spectra compared to a reference spectral library, with detection limits, recovery, and matrix effects systematically evaluated. This analytical approach provides a reliable tool for forensic and clinical toxicology, particularly in the context of the increasing interest in tryptamines for both recreational and therapeutic purposes.

articles.title: µ-QuEChERS as a Clean-Up Strategy for Determination of Ketamine, Cocaine, and Metabolites in Hair Samples.
articles.abstract: The Quick, Easy, Cheap, Effective, Rugged, and Safe (QuEChERS) method is the established approach for pesticide residue analysis in Europe and possesses the qualities required for routine application across diverse analytical fields. In forensic toxicology, the analysis often involves limited sample amounts while demanding high sensitivity to support legal proceedings. Therefore, miniaturizing a versatile and rapid method such as QuEChERS can offer a greener and more efficient alternative for routine forensic laboratories. This chapter presents two µ-QuEChERS methodologies as clean-up procedures for the determination of ketamine and norketamine, and cocaine and its metabolites, in hair samples, followed by analysis using gas chromatography coupled to tandem mass spectrometry (GC-MS/MS). Both methods achieved the cut-off values recommended by the Society of Hair Testing (SoHT).

Subacute and long-term changes in cognitive functioning after administration of classic psychedelics, MDMA and ketamine: A systematic review of clinical and preclinical evidence
articles.abstract: Psychedelic agents induce a window of heightened neuroplasticity that extends beyond acute intoxication, during which neural circuits are more amenable to change. This period may facilitate changes in cognition relevant to the treatment of psychiatric disorders. This systematic review synthesised clinical and preclinical evidence of subacute and long-term (≥1 day) effects of classic and non-classic psychedelics on cognition. MEDLINE, EMBASE, APA PsycInfo and Web of Science were searched to identify human and animal studies investigating psychedelics and cognition (executive function, attention, decision-making). Sixty-seven (47 clinical, 20 preclinical) articles met inclusion criteria. Psilocybin demonstrated the most consistent evidence of subacute and longer-term cognitive improvement, particularly in cognitive flexibility and attention. Ketamine showed enhancement across cognitive domains, although findings were heterogeneous. LSD and DMT showed no consistent subacute changes, while MDMA was associated with transient cognitive impairments that resolved within days. Risk of bias assessments revealed selective outcome reporting, poor reporting of missing data and inadequate methodological detail, limiting the confidence of findings. Current evidence provides preliminary support for subacute changes in cognition following administration of select psychedelic agents. Cognitive improvements were more frequently seen in psychiatric populations than healthy subjects, which may re

articles.title: Psychedelics and autism spectrum disorder: Mechanistic insights, translational evidence and ethical challenges
articles.abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental condition characterized by persistent deficits in social communication and interaction, restricted and repetitive patterns of behavior, and sensory processing alterations, frequently accompanied by anxiety, emotional dysregulation, and other psychiatric comorbidities. Despite advances in behavioral and pharmacological interventions, effective treatments for core ASD symptoms remain limited. Psychedelic compounds have recently emerged as potential therapeutic agents in psychiatry because of their ability to modulate serotonergic and glutamatergic signaling, enhance neuroplasticity, reorganize large-scale brain networks, and influence neurobiological pathways implicated in ASD. In this narrative review, we examine the mechanistic rationale supporting psychedelic-based approaches in ASD, including 5-HT2A receptor activation, oxytocin-serotonin interactions, excitation-inhibition dynamics, functional connectivity, and glutamatergic modulation associated with ketamine and related compounds. We also summarize current clinical and preclinical evidence involving substances such as psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide, 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine, and ketamine. Particular attention is given to the distinction between core ASD symptoms and associated symptom domains. Current evidence does not support the direct treatment of core social communication deficits or restricted and repetitive behaviors; however, psy

articles.title: Prevalence and Reasons for Microdosing Cannabis, Psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA Among U.S. Adults
articles.abstract: Microdosing involves consuming low doses of psychoactive substances, typically 1/5th to 1/20th of a recreational dose. Despite increasing public attention to cannabis and psychedelics amid evolving drug policies, epidemiological data on microdosing remain limited.A cross-sectional, web-based survey (Characterizing the Epidemiology of Cannabidiol Use Survey) of 1,525 US adults was conducted in October-November 2023 and analyzed in 2024-2025 using Ipsos KnowledgePanel. Participants reported lifetime microdosing of cannabis, psilocybin, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD), and 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA). Lifetime prevalence, frequency, and reasons for microdosing were assessed, along with associations with demographics, mental health, quality of life, and cannabis and psychedelic policy environments. Survey weights were applied to generate nationally representative estimates.Cannabis was the most commonly microdosed substance (9.4%; 95% CI=8.0, 10.7; 24.1 million adults), followed by psilocybin (5.3%; 95% CI=4.3, 6.3; 13.7 million adults), LSD (4.8%; 95% CI=3.8, 5.9; 12.4 million adults), and MDMA (2.2%; 95% CI=1.5, 2.9; 5.7 million adults). Cannabis (41.2%; 95% CI=33.3, 49.5) was primarily microdosed for medical purposes (e.g., "to manage pain"), while psilocybin (66.6%; 95% CI=56.9, 75.1), LSD (59.2%; 95% CI=46.5, 70.8) and MDMA (86.0%; 95% CI=68.8, 94.5) were more commonly microdosed for recreational purposes (e.g., "to get less high"). articles.title: Microdosing psychedelics: What, why, when, and how often? Insights from an international survey of people who use psychedelics
articles.abstract: The interest in microdosing psychedelics continues to grow within academic and recreational contexts. However, microdosing practices have changed over time, and warrants examination of use patterns within a large, global sample of consumers.The Global Psychedelic Survey 2025 (GPS 2025) was an online, anonymous, cross-sectional survey conducted from May 1-23, 2025. The survey was available in 19 languages and inquired about a wide range of topics surrounding psychedelic use. This manuscript focuses on the primary outcomes for the microdosing component of the survey, examining the substances consumed, dosing regimens employed, reasons for use, as well as the typical 'set and setting' while microdosing.In this sample, 5399 participants reported microdosing during their lifetime, of whom 69.8% (n = 3768) used a microdose within the past year. Psilocybin was the most commonly microdosed substance (n = 4377; 81.1%, 95% CI: 80.0%-82.1%), followed by LSD (n = 2136; 39.6%, 95% CI: 38.3%-40.9%). This was consistent across global regions. The 'Fadiman protocol' (i.e. one day on, two days off) was the most reported dosing regimen among regular microdosers (n = 1203; 24.3%, 95% CI: 23.1%-25.6%). While microdosing, respondents reported often spending time in nature (n = 3087; 58.9%), focusing inwards (n = 2977; 56.8%), or spending leisure time (n = 2253; 43%), demonstrating preliminary evidence supporting the integration of set and setting in the context of microdosing.This study provides

articles.title: Blinding integrity in psychedelic research: Evidence from a comparative randomized controlled trial of psilocybin, MDMA, and methylphenidate in healthy volunteers
articles.abstract: Maintaining effective blinding is a major methodological challenge in psychedelic research. This study provides a comprehensive evaluation of blinding integrity in 120 healthy volunteers who received either psilocybin, MDMA, or methylphenidate (active placebo) in a double-blind, randomized controlled trial. Using a multi-level assessment incorporating forced-choice substance guesses, certainty ratings, decision factors, and subjective substance effects, the analyses characterize blinding integrity and its relation to the substance experience. Results indicate that overall blinding was insufficient, with psilocybin showing the highest rates of functional unblinding, MDMA moderate levels, and methylphenidate the lowest. As an active placebo, methylphenidate provided more effective blinding for MDMA than for psilocybin. Incorporating certainty levels of substance guesses revealed a more differentiated pattern, with lower functional unblinding rates. Decision factors and subjective substance experiences were associated with phenomenological substance effects. Prior substance experiences did not influence accuracy of forced-choice substance guesses. These findings provide empirical guidance for the design and reporting of blinding procedures in psychedelic trials and underscore the value of systematic, multi-level assessment of blinding integrity.

articles.title: Considerations for Scaling Psychedelics: Context, Reimbursement, and the Role of the Pharmacy Benefit Manager
articles.abstract: Psychedelic therapies have shown considerable promise in clinical trials, but their effects depend heavily on context—set, setting, therapeutic relationship, and integration—in ways that sit uneasily with health care systems built to finance discrete drugs and billable services. This white paper examines the institutional pathway through which psychedelic therapies may reach patients, from regulatory approval to clinical delivery, payment, and practical access. It reviews the emerging cost-effectiveness literature and identifies three challenges for coverage: valuation (what counts as benefit), duration (the Durability–Churn and Durability–Revenue dilemmas), and delivery (labor intensity and delivery design). It describes a Context–Reimbursement Paradox: the more central context is to therapeutic effect, the harder the intervention is to translate into units that existing payment systems recognize. It then analyzes where pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) fit along a gradient of compatibility, from SSRIs to psilocybin therapy, and argues that drug pricing decisions will shape their role. It closes by considering Indigenous knowledge systems and non-medical pathways to access.

articles.title: Psilocybin and Contrasting Musical Compositions: Effects on Music-Evoked Emotional Responses in Healthy Adults
articles.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>                 <jats:p>Music is a central component of psychedelic settings, yet little experimental work has examined how psilocybin and musical composition influence music-evoked emotional responses in healthy volunteers. This exploratory, double-blind, placebo-controlled study assessed these effects during the plateau phase of psilocybin and the corresponding time window in placebo sessions following oral administration of psilocybin (0.26 mg/kg) or placebo. The study consisted of two parts. In Part 1 (n = 19), a pilot stage, the first half of participants rated music-induced affective valence for eight compositions representing different genres/subgenres (Rock/Punk, Metal/Industrial Metal, Metal/Industrial Metal, Classical/Baroque, Electronic/Dub, Folk/Nordic Folk, Electronic/Techno, Electronic/Trance, Electronic/Psytrance) using a visual analogue scale (VAS). Based on Part 1, the classical composition with the highest overall affective valence and the psytrance composition with the largest psilocybin–placebo contrast (i.e., the composition most responsive to psilocybin) were selected for Part 2 (n = 17), in which the second half of participants assessed emotional responses to music using the Geneva Emotional Music Scale (GEMS-9). Psilocybin increased wonder, transcendence, and joyful activation across both contrasting compositions. Relative to each other, the classical composition elicited greater peacefulness, tenderness, and nostalgia

articles.title: Acute psilocybin or ethocybin leads to a sustained increase in Pavlovian aversion memory in male mice
articles.abstract: <jats:p>There is considerable interest in the concept that psychedelic compounds might facilitate reorganization of emotional processing with therapeutic benefit; in particular, amelioration of excessive focus on past, current and potential-future aversive events, a dominant emotional-cognitive state in stress-related affective disorders. Translational animal models can advance understanding of specific aspects of this concept, namely, those relating to subconscious emotional memories and their neurobiology. In male mice, chronic social stress (CSS) leads to excessive tone/context-foot shock Pavlovian aversion learning (PAL) and memory (PAM), measured as time spent in freezing behavior, and provides a model for generalized excessive focus on aversion. Sub-chronic administration of SSRI antidepressant between PAL and PAM reverses the excessive PAM of CSS mice. Here we applied the model to investigate acute and sustained behavioral and neurobiological effects of psilocybin (PSY) and ethocybin (ETH). In control male mice, both psychedelics at 3 mg/kg per os resulted in 1–2 h of blood-brain exposure to the respective major metabolites psilocin and ethocin, and to head twitch responses. In the main experiment, mice underwent either 15-day CSS or control handling (CON), followed 2 days later by PAL, 1 day later by PSY, ETH or vehicle (VEH), and 3 days later by PAM testing and then brain collection. Relative to VEH, PSY and ETH led to increased PAM expression as more time spent in f

articles.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF PSILOCYBIN IN TREATMENT-RESISTANT DEPRESSION: A REVIEW
articles.abstract: <jats:p>Major depressive disorder (MDD) is one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. A substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission through standard monoaminergic therapies, meeting the clinical criteria for treatment-resistant depression (TRD). TRD is associated with significant clinical morbidity and a profound economic burden on healthcare systems. This review evaluates the clinical efficacy, safety profile, and neurobiological mechanisms of psilocybin, a serotonergic psychedelic, as a targeted intervention for TRD. Current neurobiological evidence indicates that psilocybin, upon conversion to its active metabolite psilocin, acts primarily as a 5-HT2A receptor agonist. This mechanism promotes rapid structural neuroplasticity and modulates the aberrant functional connectivity characteristic of severe depression. Recent randomized clinical trials demonstrate that psilocybin, when administered in controlled settings with psychological support, produces rapid and clinically significant reductions in depressive symptoms. Comparative data indicate that its therapeutic efficacy is at least comparable to standard first-line treatments, such as SSRIs, while frequently offering a faster onset of action. Regarding safety, psilocybin is generally well-tolerated in clinical environments; adverse events are typically mild to moderate and transient. However, the strict requirement for concurrent psychological support and rigorous psychiatric screening highlights

articles.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the ‘Psychedelic Flourishing Scale’
articles.abstract: Positive psychological changes following psychedelic experiences are widely studied, yet no validated instrument has been developed specifically to assess the breadth of enduring change that individuals attribute to those experiences. We therefore conducted a two-part programme of research to evaluate an existing measure and to develop and validate a more comprehensive scale. In Part 1, a preliminary psychometric analysis of the 11-item Mindset Questionnaire (MQ) was conducted using data from two psilocybin studies (N = 97). Its items were strongly intercorrelated (mean inter-item r = .63) and predominantly reflected a single, relatively narrow dimension of change. Part 2 followed established scale-development procedures to define the broader construct of psychedelic flourishing and develop the Psychedelic Flourishing Scale (PFS). A three-round Delphi study involving 17 experts established the construct definition and generated a 41-item pool. The PFS was then evaluated in a pre-registered cross-sectional survey of 1,296 adults who reported previous serotonergic (“classic”) psychedelic use. The sample was randomly divided for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, with the structure extracted in the exploratory half rather than specified in advance. In the confirmatory subsample, a model comprising five correlated facets showed good fit (RMSEA = .053, CFI = .965) and fitted better than a unidimensional model, although a four-factor model performed similarly.
